relations.subject: Eric John Sharpe
relations.evidence: Eric John Sharpe (19 September 1933 – 19 October 2000) was the founding Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Sydney, Australia.

relations.subject: Eric John Sharpe
relations.evidence: he presented himself as a student at the Hartley Victoria College in Manchester, as a candidate for the Methodist ministry.

relations.subject: Eric John Sharpe
relations.evidence: At the University of Manchester he achieved a B.A. (Theol.) and an M.A. degree in the History of Religions, studying under Professor S. G. F. Brandon.

relations.subject: Eric John Sharpe

relations.subject: Eric John Sharpe
relations.evidence: In 1958 he went to Sweden, where seven years later he received his doctorate in theology (Teol. Dr) in Church History with Missiology from the University of Uppsala, Sweden.

relations.subject: Eric John Sharpe
relations.evidence: he joined Prof. Brandon at the University of Manchester, England, in 1966 and then Prof. Ninian Smart at the University of Lancaster in 1970.

relations.subject: Eric John Sharpe
relations.evidence: and then Prof. Ninian Smart at the University of Lancaster in 1970.

relations.subject: Eric John Sharpe
relations.evidence: He collaborated with Ninian Smart in promoting religious studies as a subject in British schools.

relations.subject: Eric John Sharpe
relations.role: full Professor of History of Religion
relations.evidence: University of Uppsala, Sweden, where from 1978 to 1981 he held the chair as full Professor of History of Religion.

relations.subject: Eric John Sharpe
relations.evidence: In 1991 he was Senior Mission Scholar in Residence, Overseas Ministries Study Center, New Haven, Connecticut.
